items.headline: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar says Luna undercuts Chinese AI on price
items.note: Friar at Goldman's Communacopia conference on 8 Sep: an 80% cut to Luna pricing drove roughly tenfold usage, and enterprise revenue rose 32% between June and July. Direct instance of unit-price deflation raising total spend; also a live datapoint for the metered-cognition family. Figures are percentages, no dollar amounts in the piece.

items.headline: Oracle Stock Compresses Below $149 as Sept. 10 Earnings Near
items.source: TradingKey (preview); ERP Today for Q4 figures
items.note: Oracle reports Q1 FY27 on Wed 10 Sep after the close. Going in: $638bn RPO, ~$70bn FY27 capex, FY26 free cash flow of minus $23.7bn, and a ~$40bn debt-and-equity raise. Source is the preview plus June Q4 coverage, not a 24-hour story, but the print lands tomorrow and is the cleanest live test of backlog-to-cash conversion before the hyperscalers in late October. Alternative mapping: What the 10-K can't see.

items.headline: Qualcomm hands Amazon $4B of warrants to build custom silicon for AWS
items.source: The Next Web (deal reported by CNBC)
items.note: Warrants over 25m shares at $161.26, vesting in tranches tied to Amazon buying up to $60bn of Qualcomm server chips and technology, expiring 3 Sep 2036. Shares rose 4%. A supplier paying its customer in equity to lock in demand is a vivid supply-chain-dependency hook; also touches capital allocation.

items.headline: Anthropic Said to Walk Away From $6 Billion Decart Acquisition
items.note: After due diligence Anthropic dropped a ~$6bn purchase of Decart, whose software cuts the cost of training and running models by improving chip efficiency. No reason given; Bloomberg frames it as capital being kept for compute ahead of the IPO. A 'walking away' story maps to the discipline theme in the capital-allocation essay; could also feed Buffett on moats when cognition is a commodity.

items.headline: Meta Rises 6% as Muse AI Agent Arrives With Paid Subscription Tiers; Alphabet Falls 2%
items.source: 24/7 Wall St (launch covered by TechCrunch and Axios, 8 Sep)
items.note: Meta's personal agent launched 8 Sep with a free tier plus $20 and $100 monthly plans and a visible usage meter. The 24/7 piece pairs the launch with Meta's $130–145bn 2026 capex guidance and Q2 free cash flow of $784m (down from $8.55bn). A consumer-facing meter on cognition from a company whose free cash flow has nearly vanished is a strong hook for the metered-cognition essay.

items.headline: AI coding startup Cognition raises $2B at $48B valuation as revenue nears $900M
items.note: Series E led by a16z and Accel; valuation nearly doubled from $26bn in May while run-rate revenue rose from $492m to ~$900m, so the revenue multiple barely moved. Touches the valuation-of-AI-companies family and the broken-rung talent theme, but no queue title fits directly. Below the magnitude bar for a proposed title.

items.headline: Anthropic Just Committed $80B in Five Days. Here Is Who It Is Renting From.
items.source: Chamath Palihapitiya Substack (deals reported by Bloomberg; 24/7 Wall St analysis 2 Sep)
items.note: A six-year $45bn Nscale contract plus $35bn with Lambda, both neoclouds rather than hyperscalers. The underlying deals are about a week old; the 8 Sep piece is commentary. 24/7 Wall St's angle that the obligations are unfunded pending the IPO is the sharper hook: multi-year compute commitments that sit off any balance sheet until the S-1 lands. Alternative mapping: the-cognitive-supply-chain.
